Prevention: Use tolerant rice varieties, such as ‘Rok 24’ Brush and burn wild grasses around nursery sites as well as planting areas
Alternate rice with crops of different families and nutrient interest (e.g. legumes/vegetables)
Stop the migration of caterpillars to neighbouring rice plants (upland)
Monitoring: Consider treating plants with an insecticide when 10%-15% of plants per m2 show stem borer damage at 40 days after planting:
Irregular scars; Presence of dead hearts; Presence of white heads; Presence of funnel leaves; Holes in tunnelled stems
Direct Control: Up-root and destroy the infested plants by burning
Irrigate to control the larvae within the stems (Inland
Restrictions: II); Apply at flowering stage; Apply cypermethrin or alpha-cypermethrin once per planting season; To be sprayed in the morning or late in the afternoon
